progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: B1: gametes (sperm and egg) join in sexual reproduction; a gamete carries one set of chromosomes and two gametes make a full two sets; offspring must survive for a species to continue.
progression.startsWith: Coral spawning millions of eggs on the Great Barrier Reef, against a harbour seal with one egg and one pup.
progression.stopsAfter: Describing external and internal fertilisation with named animals, explaining which conditions favour each, and linking fertilisation type to egg number and parental investment in a short answer.
progression.nextLesson: B2b: how plants, fungi and microbes reproduce.

teaching.task: Explain why external fertilisers release far more eggs than internal fertilisers and relate this to parental investment.
teaching.causalExplanation: Gametes must meet, and in open water they are scattered, eaten and spread thin so huge egg numbers offset the loss; internal fertilisation protects the gametes so far fewer eggs are needed; a parent has limited energy, so many eggs with little care trades off against few young with more care.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Contrasting real animals (coral, salmon, frog, seal, hen), a trap about where fertilisation versus development happens, and an exam answer built on screen one sentence at a time.
teaching.openingDecision: Why would one animal release millions of eggs while another gets by with one?
teaching.understandingCheck: Decide the fertilisation type for a desert lizard and a sea turtle, and judge which of oysters and dugongs recovers more slowly from a storm that kills nine in ten young.
teaching.curriculumScope: Describe the mechanisms of reproduction in animals, comparing external and internal fertilisation and their link to egg number and parental investment (BIO12-12, Module 5). Meiosis, haploid and diploid, pregnancy and plants are deferred to later lessons.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, painted animal plates with coded gamete fields, seesaw balance and answer cards.
design.transitionPlan: Push-through from the coral plate to the seal plate; the board splits into outside and inside columns; plates change one animal at a time; the dot field dims as the internal fertilisation view arrives; scene crossfades with settle.

scenes.visualReference: Painted coral spawning plate and harbour seal with pup plate
scenes.teachingReason: Sets a striking contrast to motivate the question
scenes.narrationCue: millions of tiny eggs / harbour seal / a single egg / a single pup
scenes.motionPurpose: Egg cloud swells over the coral, then a push-through shows the seal with one dot for one egg
scenes.onScreenChange: Egg cloud swells over the reef on "millions of tiny eggs"; push-through to the seal plate on "harbour seal"; one egg dot on "a single egg" and a scribble circle round the pup on "a single pup"; heading writes on
scenes.holdPurpose: Brief look at the seal and pup

scenes.visualReference: Coded sperm, egg and zygote strips on a plain board
scenes.teachingReason: Introduces fertilisation, the zygote and the meeting problem, reusing B1 wording
scenes.narrationCue: one set of chromosomes / half of the instructions / joins / zygote / two main ways
scenes.motionPurpose: Gamete strips fill half an instruction bar each and complete inside one zygote cell when the sperm joins
scenes.onScreenChange: Each gamete shows one chromosome strip on "one set of chromosomes"; the strips fill halves of an instruction bar on "half of the instructions"; the sperm travels in and the bar completes inside one cell labelled "zygote" on "joins"; pin, short path and drying droplet doodles draw on the three problems; the board splits into two columns on "two main ways"

scenes.visualReference: Droplet and swimming sperm icons, then coral, frog pond and salmon plates in turn
scenes.teachingReason: Shows what external fertilisation is and why water is needed
scenes.narrationCue: water matters for two reasons / sea / pond / gravel
scenes.motionPurpose: Two reason icons draw, then three animal plates appear one at a time with place chips collecting on a rail
scenes.onScreenChange: A droplet and a swimming sperm draw on "two reasons"; the coral spawn cloud appears on "sea", the frog pond plate on "pond", and salmon eggs and a sperm trail in the gravel on "gravel"; place chips collect on the rail

scenes.visualReference: Coral, salmon and frog plates again with moon, scent-wave and calendar doodles
scenes.teachingReason: Shows how external fertilisers get gametes into the same place and time
scenes.narrationCue: same few nights / scent / same place / clasps / right over the eggs
scenes.motionPurpose: The coral cloud crowds into one patch, a scent wave guides salmon to one gravel bed, and the frog pair is pushed in on for the clasp
scenes.onScreenChange: A moon chip and the cloud crowding into one patch on "same few nights"; a scent wave from the river mouth and fish converging on one bed on "scent" and "same place"; the camera pushes to the clasping frogs on "clasps" and the sperm trail lands on the spawn on "right over the eggs"
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold the frog pair with the sperm on the spawn

scenes.visualReference: Coded field of hundreds of gamete dots over water with current and fish silhouettes
scenes.teachingReason: Shows two separate kinds of loss and why huge numbers answer them
scenes.narrationCue: sweep / eat / spread so thin / four thousand to fourteen thousand / a few still make it
scenes.motionPurpose: Dots shear away, fish remove dots, the few pairs become eggs and most of those fade, leaving a handful circled
scenes.onScreenChange: Dots shear sideways on "sweep"; fish silhouettes remove dots on "eat"; dots fade apart on "spread so thin"; the egg count chip ticks on at the number; only a handful stay lit and are circled on "a few still make it"; the rule line writes on

scenes.visualReference: Painted bearded dragon cut-away on dry sand beside the dimmed dot field from the odds scene
scenes.teachingReason: Shows how internal fertilisation protects gametes so far fewer eggs are needed
scenes.narrationCue: inside the female's body / short distance / far fewer eggs / plenty of sperm / sharks / find each other
scenes.motionPurpose: A sperm path draws inside the female while the dot field dims, then a male silhouette and two approaching animals show what stays costly
scenes.onScreenChange: A sperm path draws inside the female and ends at the egg on "inside the female's body", with a circle on "short distance"; the earlier dot field dims with a "far fewer eggs" chip; a sperm cloud stays beside a male on "plenty of sperm"; a shark icon pops on "sharks"; two silhouettes meet on "find each other"

scenes.visualReference: Hen cut-away plate, then a coded location grid with hen, seal and frog crops
scenes.teachingReason: Corrects the idea that egg laying means external fertilisation
scenes.narrationCue: inside the hen / before the shell forms / hen / seal / frog
scenes.motionPurpose: A sperm travels up the oviduct, the shell draws on after it, and a grid fills row by row with the hen row circled
scenes.onScreenChange: A sperm travels to the yolk on "inside the hen" and the shell draws on after it on "before the shell forms"; the two-column grid writes on and the hen, seal and frog rows fill as each is named; the hen row is circled in amber

scenes.visualReference: Coded cause strip, seesaw balance with salmon and seal plates, buried-egg doodle
scenes.teachingReason: Explains the trade-off between egg number and parental investment and its limits
scenes.narrationCue: limited supply / thousands of eggs / single pup / parental investment / some reptiles
scenes.motionPurpose: A fixed energy bar splits between eggs and care, and the seesaw tilts from the salmon side to the seal side
scenes.onScreenChange: The cause strip draws phrase by phrase; the energy bar draws on "limited supply"; the salmon side fills with egg dots on "thousands of eggs" and a crossed parent icon appears; the seal side fills with one pup on "single pup"; the seesaw tilts on "or"; a buried-egg doodle labelled "trend, not a rule" appears on "some reptiles"

scenes.visualReference: Question card and a chain of four written answer cards with salmon and seal icons
scenes.teachingReason: Models how to build a linked explain answer one sentence at a time
scenes.motionPurpose: Four answer cards land in turn, the word because is circled on three of them and earlier cards shrink to the top rail
scenes.onScreenChange: The question card writes on with "explain" underlined; the cause, effect, contrast and link cards land on their cue words; "because" is circled on the first three and the linking word underlined in a second colour; earlier cards shrink to the rail
scenes.holdPurpose: Hold the four cards to read

scenes.visualReference: Two rows: a coded seal colony and a coded cod population with a dense egg cloud
scenes.teachingReason: Shows that few young per adult means slow recovery from equal losses
scenes.narrationCue: storm year / survive / how many young each adult adds / rebuilds slowly / rebuild faster
scenes.motionPurpose: Nine in ten young are slashed in both rows, the adults stay lit, and the cod refill dial fills quickly while the seal dial creeps
scenes.onScreenChange: Red slashes remove nine in ten young in both rows on "storm year" while the adults stay lit on "survive"; "adds next year" chips show about 1 for seals and millions for cod; the seal refill dial creeps on "rebuilds slowly" and the cod dial fills on "rebuild faster"

scenes.visualReference: Three painted vignettes: desert lizard, sea turtle nest, and oysters beside a dugong with calf
scenes.teachingReason: Unseen transfer with every condition visible, including that the adults survive in both populations
scenes.motionPurpose: Countdown ring runs through the answer-free thinking hold
scenes.onScreenChange: Three numbered vignettes appear as each situation is named; the storm and surviving-adults conditions stay on the board; the countdown ring starts after the narration
scenes.holdPurpose: Quiet answer-free thinking hold with countdown

scenes.visualReference: Same three vignettes with verdict stamps, sperm paths and the seesaw and refill dials
scenes.teachingReason: Explains each answer and names the lays-eggs, beach and lost-eggs slips
scenes.narrationCue: internal / inside the female / dugong / oysters
scenes.motionPurpose: Each vignette gets a verdict stamp and reason card, with a sperm path inside the lizard and turtle and the slow dugong dial against the fast oyster dial
scenes.onScreenChange: The lizard gets an "internal" stamp with a sperm path inside; the turtle shows a sperm path inside her and an "inside, before the eggs were laid" stamp; the dugong dial creeps while the oyster dial fills; amber doodles mark each trap

scenes.visualReference: Aid written large with wave, dot cloud, animal pair and shield icons and the hen
scenes.teachingReason: Gives a reusable summary aid and hands off to plants, fungi and microbes
scenes.narrationCue: External / Internal / where they meet / Next
scenes.motionPurpose: The aid writes on in two halves with icons, then the trap line and the next chip appear
scenes.onScreenChange: The "External" half writes on with a wave and dot cloud, then the "Internal" half with the pair and shield; the trap line writes on beside the hen; the next-lesson chip appears

scenes.visualReference: Key notes card with the memory aid in large writing
scenes.motionPurpose: Notes appear then stay still for copying
scenes.holdPurpose: Quiet copy hold with pause invitation
